subject: Career
title: The Elevator Pitch Formula
description: One-minute skill: The Elevator Pitch Formula.

hook.text: 'So, what do you do?' You have eight seconds before attention fades. Make them count.

buildup.text: Most people answer with their job title. 'I'm a product manager.' That's a label, not a pitch.

discovery.text: The formula: 'I help [audience] achieve [outcome] by [method].' Problem-focused, not title-focused.

twist.text: 'I help e-commerce brands increase conversions through data-driven UX.' Now they're curious.

climax.text: Practice until it feels natural. Rehearsed should sound conversational, not robotic.

punchline.text: Don't say what you are. Say what you solve.

quiz.question: What's the most effective elevator pitch structure?

details.summary: An effective elevator pitch distills who you are, what you do, and why it matters into thirty to sixty seconds of compelling speech. The best pitches focus on the value you create for others rather than listing your credentials.
details.whyItMatters: Opportunities arise unexpectedly. A polished elevator pitch ensures you can articulate your value at any moment, from networking events to casual encounters.
takeaways: Structure as problem, solution, and proof in thirty to sixty seconds
Focus on the value you create rather than your job title
Practice until the delivery sounds natural, not rehearsed

faq.question: How do you tailor your elevator pitch for different audiences?
faq.answer: Keep the core value proposition consistent but adjust the language and emphasis for the audience. For technical audiences, lead with specific expertise. For executives, lead with business impact. For peers, lead with how your skills complement theirs.

faq.question: What is the biggest mistake people make in their elevator pitch?
faq.answer: Making it about themselves rather than the value they provide. Listing credentials bores listeners. Describing how you solve a problem they care about captures attention. Shift from 'I am a data scientist' to 'I help companies find hidden revenue in their data.'
